questions.question_english: A newly appointed school bus driver possesses a valid heavy vehicle license and five years of experience. However, the transport contractor has not yet completed his police verification. The school is short of drivers. What should the Principal do?
options_english: Allow the driver to operate the bus temporarily until the verification is done.
Instruct a senior teacher or staff member to personally accompany the driver on all bus routes in lieu of formal police verification documentation.
Prohibit the driver from operating the bus until police verification is completed and documented.

questions.explanation_english: Prohibit the driver from operating the bus until police verification is completed and documented. Permitting unverified personnel to operate student transportation compromises safety and violates mandatory safety guidelines. Despite valid driving credentials and staff shortages, police verification documentation must be completed prior to duty assignment. Enforcing strict pre-employment verification standards prevents unauthorized contact, minimizes risk, and maintains institutional accountability regarding student transportation security.

Conducting psychological assessments acts as a preventive safety layer, minimizing risks of child abuse or misconduct and ensuring a safe social environment in schools.
